text:
Diego Alvarez: Hey team, Diego here (starting tomorrow on SecEng). Quick Notion question: I can view the team's runbook and the security postmortem template but everything is read-only. I need to duplicate the runbook, remove some org-specific links, and share an editable version with my manager. Who owns these templates and what's the cleanest request format to get page-level edit rights? Also curious if duplicating breaks any on-call automations.

devex: Welcome Diego! Canonical security runbooks live under Redwood > Eng > Security > Runbooks. The owners are listed in the right-hand properties. For temporary edits we give page-level Editor (preferred) rather than workspace Editor. Please DM @devex with: 1) full Notion URL 2) your SSO email 3) duration (e.g., 14 days) and what you'll change.

docs-bot: Note: duplicating a page preserves database properties, but external automations (PagerDuty, Slack webhooks, Zapier) often reference the canonical page ID. If you plan to duplicate and keep automations, ping sec-eng to re-register hooks or keep edits on the canonical page.

Diego Alvarez: Got it — thanks. Two clarifying Qs: (1) If I duplicate and move the copy into Team > SecEng > Drafts, will the page-level integrations still point to the old page? (2) Is there a recommended field to indicate a page is a dev copy vs canonical?

sec-eng (Avery): Good q. Integrations usually target page IDs, so a moved copy will not inherit the webhook bindings. We keep a small `Meta` property on runbooks: `SourcePage` (URL) + `Status` (Draft/Canonical). For drafts, set `Status` = Draft and add `SourcePage` with the original URL. That helps our automation to ignore drafts.

Miriam Ortiz: If you want managers to edit but not break webhooks, ask for Editor on the canonical page and make your changes inside the canonical in a new section called "Draft - <Date>". Then sec-eng can re-run any integration checks before promoting. Example request format that speeds things up:
```
@devex please add Editor on https://redwood.notion.so/Sec-Runbook-xyz for:
- Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.com)
Duration: 14 days
Reason: copy and sanitize links for new hire onboarding
```

People Ops (Hannah): Also if you're sanitizing links that contain internal HR data, double-check before publishing. For anything that references employee PII, remove it or replace with placeholders. If you'd like, file a quick review with People Ops and tag me and sec-eng and we'll do a 1-hour review.

Diego Alvarez: Thanks everyone. Final thing 11: is there a naming convention to make drafts discoverable and excluded from search/automation? I don't want my draft to accidentally be used in an incident.

docs-bot: Naming convention we use: prefix drafts with `DRAFT - <ShortTitle> - <Initials> - <YYYYMMDD>`. Also add page property `Status=Draft` and `Visibility=Cohort/Team/Private`. Our incident playbooks automation ignores pages with `Status=Draft` or names starting with `DRAFT -`.

Miriam Ortiz: One last tip: when duplicating templates that include database tables, click into the duplicated DB -> View menu -> Make sure the default view filters exclude `Status=Archived`. Sometimes copies bring over saved filters that hide critical columns.

Diego Alvarez: Perfect. I'll DM @devex the page link and my SSO, duplicate into Team > SecEng > Drafts with the DRAFT prefix, set Status=Draft and SourcePage, and ask People Ops for a quick review on any HR-related links. Appreciate the fast help! :wave:
